My top 10:

  1. Golden State Warriors

  6. Indiana Pacers

Spurs, Cavs, Thunder, Clippers, Warriors.

Spurs and Cavs are the deepest teams so I think even if injuries take a toll, they can overcome them.

I think KD being a #2 threat is very good for him. He might put up less points but I think he'll show up bigger in the big moments than he has. If everyone can stay healthy they can be really scary, but I don't see them all staying healthy.

I really like Clippers roster. They have a lot of guys at the 2/3 who can score a lot of points but who play with seemingly no consistency. If they can keep Paul warm until playoffs I think they easily make a run. Griffin only gets better every year so I like their chances.

Warriors did a lot of things last season that I'm not sure are repeatable and with Steve Kerr being in or out for awhile they will struggle more. Last year they stayed healthy, and I don't think that luck continues either. I don't think they got better this offseason and imo when you don't get better you're getting worse.

KD at number 2 option? I think that's a sure way of seeing him leave. He is number one, and should always be number one.

While Westbrook can be number 1, he shouldn't be. KD is always a mismatch, regardless of who is guarding him. This makes it necessary for the offense to run through KD, making him the number 1 option at all times.
I think he leaves regardless. KD gets cold and he doesn't always play big which are my only criticisms of him. I think as a #2 you'll see much less of that side of him.

I think it's fair to think that the Warriors aren't going to win this year, my thoughts about them is they didn't lose anyone major and they are by far the best shooting team in the league. Problem with them is that they take a LOT of shots quickly and if they are off even a little bit they are going to lose. There is no backup plan with them.

Spurs are probably my #1 "Team least likely to surprise you". Just you know what to expect with them.

I just don't think they will shoot as well this year as they did last year. I think you're going to see regression.

Spurs remind a bit of your Colts. The veterans they picked and already have look great on paper because of their name, but there's no telling how they are all going to play together. I'm a believer though.
